answer:
Split the question in two, because the honest answers differ.

1) The consultation as an episode in the landscape's history: IN SCOPE, and worth recording. A public consultation is an intentional action by an actor that changed the state of the social system around the site, which is exactly E7 Activity (there is no CRM subclass for 'consultation', so type it with P2 has type against a local/AAT term). Model it as: the consultation E7 Activity, P14 carried out by the trust, P4 has time-span the consultation window, P16 used specific object the road scheme. The scheme itself has not been built, so it is not an event at all; it exists only as a documented plan, i.e. E29 Design or Procedure ('documented plans for the execution of actions... An independent intellectual product that may have never been applied'). The report or dataset the platform produced is an E31 Document, P70 documents the consultation activity (P70 is quantified as necessary on E31) and P129 is about the scheme. If the trust later decides to route, redesign or abandon the road, that decision is another E7 Activity with P17 was motivated by the consultation - that link is genuinely part of the landscape's documented history and is the main reason to bother recording the consultation at all.

2) The payload you actually asked about - the 58/24/18 percentages, the count of 1,340, and 'anonymous public sentiment' as a queryable fact: OUT OF SCOPE as modelled data. Four independent findings converge:

- The specification's own Intended Scope explicitly excludes this family of data: information required solely for the administration and management of cultural institutions, 'personnel, accounting, and visitor statistics, falls outside the Intended Scope of the CIDOC CRM' (Introduction > Scope of the CIDOC CRM). Aggregate counts of anonymous members of the public responding to an operational planning exercise are the same kind of thing as visitor statistics. I am drawing that analogy; the SIG has never ruled on consultations specifically.
- Modelling principles > Extensions of CIDOC CRM says the CRM prioritises facts one would want to retrieve across heterogeneous institutions and does not focus on 'the administrative practices internal to an institution'.
- There is no apparatus to hang the numbers on. connect E7 E54 returns no dimension property at all - an E7 Activity cannot carry an E54 Dimension. connect E31 E54 offers P43 has dimension, but the tool prints its full path, which runs through E18 Physical Thing and E16 Measurement: it is a shortcut for measuring a physical thing. E16 Measurement is restricted to values determined by a 'systematic, objective procedure of direct observation of particular states of physical reality', which a tally of opinions is not. So E54/E16 would be a misuse, not a stretch.
- The CRM has no construct for an attitude or preference held by an unidentified aggregate. The nearest thing in the family, CRMinf I2 Belief, is the period in which an actor holds a proposition set to a belief value - true, false or in between - which is about truth, not about approval. Work on CRMsoc, where social phenomena of this kind would have lived, was discontinued (Issue 580).

What to do instead: keep the figures, but keep them as content of the document rather than as facts in the graph. Put the tallies in P190 has symbolic content or P3 has note on the E31 Document, and let the document's P70 documents link tie them to the consultation event. The CRM's own criterion for when to structure something is in the E13 Attribute Assignment scope note: whether a statement is documented 'explicitly in structures of a schema rather than free text, depends on whether this information should be accessible by structured queries'. Nobody is going to run a cross-institutional query for '58% opposed', so free text is the correct level.

The free-text comments are the one part of the sentiment data that does have a proper home: if the trust retains them verbatim, each comment is an E33 Linguistic Object with P72 has language and P190 has symbolic content, P129 is about the parkland or the scheme. That records them as texts that exist, which is true and useful, without asserting that the parkland has a property called 'public feeling'. Do not aggregate the authors into an E74 Group: a Group requires members who 'act collectively or in a similar way due to any form of unifying relationship', and 1,340 unconnected respondents are exactly the 'coincidental aggregation' that Issue 247 decided need not be given a persistent identity.

One further caution from Modelling principles > Authorship of Knowledge Base Contents: statements entered plainly into a knowledge base are by default the maintaining team's own. Recording 'the road is disliked' as a bare fact would make the trust the author of that claim. Attaching it as the content of a named E31 Document keeps the authorship where it belongs - with the consultation platform's report.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: Its scope note limits it to values determined by a 'systematic, objective procedure of direct observation of particular states of physical reality', and P39 measured is quantified as necessary with range E18 Physical Thing. Counting how many people ticked 'opposed' observes no physical state and measures no physical thing.

connect E7 E54 returns no dimension property, so the response count cannot attach to the consultation event at all. On the report, connect E31 E54 offers P43 has dimension but prints its full path as running through E18 Physical Thing and E16 Measurement - it is a shortcut for a measurement of a physical thing, not a slot for arbitrary statistics.

rejected_alternatives.option: E74 Group (for the respondents, or for 'the 58% opposed')
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E74 requires individuals who 'act collectively or in a similar way due to any form of unifying relationship'. Anonymous respondents who happened to click the same option share no unifying relationship and never acted together. Issue 247 settled that coincidental aggregations need not be assigned an individual persistent identity.

rejected_alternatives.option: E13 Attribute Assignment (to make the tally a queryable assertion)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E13 records an assertion about one property of an object or a single relation between two items. '58% opposed' is not a property of the landscape or of the scheme, and its own scope note makes explicit structuring conditional on whether the information needs to be reachable by structured queries. It is not, so free text on the report is the right level. E13 would only earn its place if the trust needed to query the trust's own assertion of the outcome against a rival tally.

I2 is the period during which an actor holds an I4 Proposition Set to have an I6 Belief Value - true, false or in between. Opposition to a road is a preference, not a judgement about the truth of a proposition, so the belief value has nothing to range over.

rejected_alternatives.option: E5 Event / E7 Activity for the road construction itself
rejected_alternatives.why_not: The road has not been built. The CRM documents what happened; the only thing that exists is the plan, hence E29. The gap for planned-but-unexecuted activity is a known one - an 'Activity Plan' subclass of E29 was proposed in 2009 (t0483) and never adopted, E101 Intention to Apply is no longer defined in v7.1.3, and CRMsoc was discontinued (Issue 580).

siblings_considered.why_not: E63 Beginning of Existence is the other branch under E5 alongside E7. The consultation is not the coming-into-being of a persistent item - the compiling of the report would be an E65 Creation, which is both E7 and E63, but the consultation itself is a plain intentional action by the trust with no persistent item brought into existence, so the E7 level is correct.

E36 Visual Item is the right class for the conceptual content of the scheme's drawings, and the trust may well hold those too. But what the consultation put before the public and what needs recording is the plan of action - a schema for activities that may never be executed - which is E29's business, not the recognisable marks and images of any one drawing.

The consultation report is used here precisely because it makes propositions about reality: it is what carries P70 documents, quantified as necessary on E31, linking the figures to the event they came from. E33 Linguistic Object would record it merely as a text and would impose P72 has language while dropping the documentary relation, which is the whole point of holding it.

An individual comment such as one saying the road would ruin the feel of the place is an expression in natural language, not an identifiable item whose purpose is to make propositions about reality; treating it as E31 Document would oblige it to carry P70 documents, asserting that an anonymous complaint documents something. E33 with P190 has symbolic content records the text as it stands without endorsing it.

notes: The decisive evidence was easy to reach once found, but two tool behaviours slowed it down. First, docs prints only a ~300-character snippet by default and --raw does not change that; only --json returns full chunk text, and the Intended Scope exclusion of 'personnel, accounting, and visitor statistics' sits past the snippet boundary, so a normal docs search never shows it. Second, 'show' does not accept document chunk ids (only message ids), so there is no direct way to read a chunk you have located other than re-querying with --json. The 'Full path' now printed by connect was what settled the E54 question - P43 has dimension looks applicable to E31 until you see it expand into a measurement of an E18 Physical Thing. Confidence is medium rather than high because the archive contains no SIG discussion of public consultation, stakeholder opinion or survey data at all; the visitor-statistics exclusion is a close analogy I am drawing, not a ruling the SIG made about this case.
